data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR prebuilt binary package with all sources pinned to SHA256 checksums from the official upstream GitHub repository (github.com/metantesan/mitsuzo). The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable definitions and a package() function that installs binaries, man pages, and license files to appropriate system directories. No executable code runs during sourcing, no suspicious network requests or code execution patterns exist, and all downloaded artifacts are integrity-verified. The 'inconclusive' result from qwen3-235b was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing mitsuzo.1, not by any security concern. Two other models successfully audited all files including mitsuzo.1 (a standard troff man page) and found no issues.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from an infrastructure failure, not a security judgment. The qwen3-235b model encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit mitsuzo.1, causing it to return 'inconclusive'. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully audited the same file and correctly identified it as a standard man page with no malicious content. This is a tool error, not a genuine disagreement about package safety.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to audit mitsuzo.1 due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors during file audits should trigger automatic retries rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive
The tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to infrastructure error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' in its verdict logic
When one model fails on a file due to API error but other models successfully audit that same file, the successful audits should resolve the coverage gap
